000
FXUS63 KIWX 050929
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
529 AM EDT Mon Oct 5 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Primarily dry conditions are expected through this work week.

- After starting out with slightly below normal high temps,
  highs slightly above normal take over for the end of the work
  week.

- Cold Tuesday morning with lows dipping down to the 30s for
  some areas north of US-6.


&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 426 AM EDT Mon Oct 5 2026

Pretty uneventful period this week with the biggest impacts
being the cool, brisk mornings with patches of light fog/mist
possible each morning. The coldest morning is expected overnight
tonight into Tuesday morning with lows in the low 40s to upper 
30s especially north of US-6. A few patches of light frost 
especially on metal vehicles or roof tops may be possible in 
these same areas but at this time dew points look to stay warm 
enough for mainly dew covering of surfaces. Will continue to 
monitor as stated previously if a bit drier airmass is able to 
push far enough south into the area that lower lows would be 
possible. Still stressing that if you have temperature sensitive
plants/animals it would be best to protect them out of an 
abundance of caution.

Dry conditions continue through the work week and next chances
of precipitation look to come by late weekend. High 
temperatures this week will start out below normal and trend 
warmer through the week to more slightly above normal levels 
(low to mid 70s). Just for reference current normal high 
temperatures at Fort Wayne is currently at 69 degrees and 67 for
South Bend.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z TAFS THROUGH 12Z TUESDAY/... 
Issued at 529 AM EDT Mon Oct 5 2026

VFR conditions are expected at the terminals. 

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory until 11 AM EDT this morning for LMZ043-
     046.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Andersen
AVIATION...MCD

spc.text:
SPC AC 050557

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1257 AM CDT Mon Oct 05 2026

   Valid 051200Z - 061200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are unlikely today.

   ...Synopsis...
   Upper ridging and accompanying mid-level northwesterly flow will
   dominate most of the CONUS as a pronounced mid-level trough
   overspreads New England and ejects into the Atlantic today. Surface
   high pressure and large-scale subsidence will overspread much of the
   U.S. east of the MS River while surface troughing becomes
   established across the Great Plains, but with limited moisture. The
   net result will be limited thunderstorm development over much of the
   CONUS. Along the Gulf Coast into FL, a few thunderstorms may develop
   ahead of a diffuse frontal boundary given the presence of seasonable
   low-level moisture. A couple of lightning flashes may also accompany
   a few mid-level impulses over the Great Basin, Rockies, Upper MS
   Valley, and northern New England in association with localized
   ascent and cooler temperatures aloft.

   ..Squitieri/Wendt.. 10/05/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

SPC AC 050443

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1143 PM CDT Sun Oct 04 2026

   Valid 061200Z - 071200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are not expected Tuesday.

   ...Synopsis...
   On Tuesday, a deep upper trough will eject northeastward out of the
   Maritimes and New England, with a secondary low-amplitude trough
   pushing across Ontario and the Upper Great Lakes through Tuesday
   night. A large area of high pressure will encompass much of the
   eastern states, preventing much destabilization ahead of the Great
   Lakes system. Even so, weak elevated instability may support
   isolated weak thunderstorms over Michigan late.

   To the south, thunderstorms will again be likely over the Gulf of
   America into central and southern Florida as northeast surface winds
   push a cold front farther south. Weak shear and lapse rates will
   preclude severe weather chances over Florida.

   Elsewhere, scattered storms are expected over the eastern Great
   Basin and into western Colorado, as a pocket of cooler midlevel
   temperatures with a weak upper wave moves across the area. Severe
   storms are unlikely, though locally strong gusts cannot be ruled out
   during the afternoon due to the dry sub-cloud layer.

   ..Jewell.. 10/05/2026

spc.text:
SPC AC 050639

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0139 AM CDT Mon Oct 05 2026

   Valid 071200Z - 081200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are unlikely on Wednesday.

   ...Synopsis...
   An upper low will be situated near James Bay on Wednesday, with a
   broad upper trough enveloping much of eastern Canada. A strong upper
   speed max and tight midlevel temperature gradient will extend
   roughly from MN to the Great Lakes, with gradual height falls across
   the region. Meanwhile, a southern-stream upper jet will extend from
   the Desert Southwest into TX, and across the Gulf Coast states. Cool
   midlevel temperatures aloft will be prevalent over the Four Corners
   states with -12 C at 500 mb.

   Minimal instability will be present to support any thunderstorms
   from the Great Lakes into the Northeast, despite the cooling aloft,
   as surface temperatures will be relatively cool. A few low-topped
   showers may affect the Lower Great Lakes Wednesday night.

   Isolated thunderstorms will again be possible over the FL Peninsula,
   as a front and surface trough gradually move south. Instability and
   shear will be weak enough to preclude any severe weather chances.

   Elsewhere, daytime heating and the presence of cool temperatures
   aloft will support scattered afternoon showers and thunderstorms
   over parts of UT, CO, AZ and NM. Isolated evening/overnight
   thunderstorms may extend into NE, as southwest 850 mb winds develop
   over the central Plains, aiding meager moisture advection. Severe
   storms appear unlikely.

   ..Jewell.. 10/05/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
